questions.q: The section **Silicon Isolation Decisions** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A static-partitioning hypervisor binds cores, memory, and peripherals to isolated partitions at boot and colors caches, the standard pattern for a real-time enclave on a shared die.
WCET comes from static analysis, measurement plus margin, hybrid methods, or probabilistic tail models, and local worst cases do not compose to a global one on modern microarchitectures.

Memory arbiters schedule bursts, not averages, so a safety read waits on the backlog ahead of it and the controller's policy, and shared-cache miss handling, not bandwidth, threatens the declared bound.

The placement record binds the declared WCET and deadline to the execution domain, privilege, period, unloaded and loaded maxima, bus QoS, droop and thermal limits, mitigations, and the conditions left untested.
